identity.name: The One-Number Baby Budget
identity.subtitle: A first-year household money system that replaces cart panic and silent shortfalls with one trusted budget number, a Buy/Wait/Never list, and a 30-day use audit.
identity.one_line_promise: A written first-year budget both partners follow — so every baby purchase has a place, and nothing essential is missed for lack of a number.
identity.journey_position: m01 first-year household money; entry point — onward journey links pending

customer.target_person: Expecting and first-year parents facing new baby costs while household income is paused, shrunk or unpredictable, with no trusted budget number.
customer.situation: New recurring costs collide with shrunken income every month without a single trusted number, so every purchase is feared and every bill restarts the fight.
customer.trigger: Her salary stopped but the bills did not, and the hospital asked for a deposit before admission.
constraints: No trusted single budget number; prices vary by market, week, tier and pack size.
Irregular income months make any fixed monthly budget fail.
Provider-role pressure and family purchase expectations punish admitting shortfalls.
customer.emotional_stake: Wants to prove competence as a mother by providing without ruin, and to feel like a smart mother rather than a guilty one.

before_state.summary: No first-year budget exists; money disappears into feared purchases and re-added carts while the couple fights over baby spending.

after_state.summary: The household states one trusted budget number and keeps a baby fund; the budget chart is posted and followed, and unused purchases are resold.

mechanism.core: Turn an feared, unmeasured stream of baby spending into one trusted budget number plus a standing Buy/Wait/Never discipline and a 30-day use audit.
mechanisms: A real baby budget quiz converts unknown spending into one stated number both partners can see.
Buy/Wait/Never classification stops fear-buying before money leaves the household.
A 30-day use audit plus resell converts mistaken purchases back into fund money.
Corner-shop cost-swaps replace three weekly overspends with planned buys.
mechanism.why_it_should_work: The recurring failure is not irresponsibility but the absence of a number: with no trusted total, every purchase is judged in isolation and fear decides. A posted number, a classification rule and a dated audit replace isolated fear-decisions with a visible system.

path.objective: Run the real baby budget quiz tonight and post the one-number budget chart on the fridge.
Sort every planned purchase into the Buy, Wait and Never list before spending.
Keep the thirty-day use audit log and resell whatever the baby never used.
Use the corner-shop cost-swap card that replaces three weekly overspends with planned buys.

first_win.action: Delete the fear-items from the cart and capture the first budget snapshot: one number, three swaps, tonight.

failure_map.see: TR-PPL-FAMILY-MONEY-001 failure_point_map (cart-delete loop; no trusted number; irregular income)

rescue_protocols.see: TR-PPL-FAMILY-MONEY-001 failure_point_map rescue protocols (specified assets pending build)

reentry.protocol: Restart the current audit cycle from the budget chart; re-run the quiz only if income or household shape changed.

maintenance.system: Keep the posted budget chart and the 30-day audit as the standing default after the measurement window.

individual_progress_metrics: Decision clarity: the household can state one trusted first-year budget number.
A completed Buy/Wait/Never classification covering the planned purchases.
A documented first-year cost range with source dates.
A completed 30-day use audit with resell actions logged.

voice.formality: plain and direct; no corporate or motivational register
voice.directness: high; name the number and the next action
voice.technical_depth: everyday arithmetic only; no financial jargon
voice.cultural_context: Situation-first language; household and market realities taken from the customer's own inputs. Cultural and family dynamics (provider-role pressure, elder purchase expectations, ceremony obligations) surface only where relevant to that customer's reality — never as default decoration, never erased where material.
voice.terminology: amounts in the customer's selected currency, always with date, place and tier; Buy/Wait/Never; one number; audit
voice.reading_level: plain everyday language; short sentences; no financial literacy assumed
voice.first_second_person: second-person practical — you and your household
